proof_summary: Partitioning by subset size, a roots-of-unity filter shows that the count for size \(k\) differs from \(\binom nk/k\) by an exponentially smaller amount, using factorization into complete root-of-unity blocks to bound the nontrivial Fourier coefficients. The resulting main sum is rewritten as \(\sum_{j\le n}(2^j-1)/j\); reflecting it about \(j=n\), expanding \(1/(n-i)\) through degree five, and evaluating the geometric moments \(\sum i^t2^{-i}\) yields the stated coefficients, while geometric tail and remainder bounds are negligible.
